newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on exports and snow cover.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on exports and snow cover.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on bearish export news plus prospects for a snow cover in at least part of the U.S. winter wheat growing region which will protect the crop from suffering severe winterkill, traders said.
"Exports were bearish and the concern over winterkill was overblown," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
USDA early Thursday said net export sales of U.S. wheat during the week ended January 2 totaled a minus 66,700 tonnes, well below trade expectations for 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
The sales reduction was tied to cancellations by unknown destinations as well as by Trinidad and Mexico, USDA said.
Wheat futures were boosted earlier this week on fears some of the U.S. wheat crop would be harmed by cold temperatures and lack of snow cover.
Now there is an insulating blanket of snow falling in key U.S. winter growing regions which will prevent freeze-damage to the crop.
Weather Services Corp's Peter Leavitt said early Thursday "there will be plenty of talk about winterkill but the reality is, it won't have much impact."
Wheat closed two to 5-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 5-3/4 at $3.89-1/4.
Merrill Lynch Futures sold two million bushels of March, Term Commodities sold one million March and Refco Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 13,488 contracts traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 200 March $4.10 calls at 6-1/4 to 6-1/2 cents, Refco Inc sold 200 March $4.00 calls at 8-3/4 cents, Cargill Investor Services sold 200 May $3.40 calls and sold 200 May $3.40 puts at 39 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, below the 10,031 traded Wednesday.
